question: Can I Require Manual Approval Before an Order Is Confirmed?
metaDescription: Yes, commonly by defaulting new orders to On Hold and only moving them forward after a manual review — a plugin can formalize this workflow.
shortAnswer: Yes, the common approach is defaulting new orders (or those meeting specific conditions) to On Hold rather than immediately Processing, giving staff a review point before the order proceeds to fulfillment or, in the case of a payment method that hasn't yet captured funds, before capturing payment at all. A dedicated order-approval plugin can formalize this into a clearer workflow with explicit approve/reject actions rather than relying purely on status conventions.

bodyHtml:
Why Some Stores Need This

Not every order should proceed automatically — a wholesale/B2B store might want to verify pricing or availability before confirming a large order, a store selling customizable or made-to-order products might want to confirm feasibility first, and some businesses want a fraud-review step before capturing payment on higher-risk orders. WooCommerce's flexible status system supports this, though it needs deliberate configuration rather than being a single settings toggle.

How to Set This Up

  • Default new orders to On Hold rather than the normal automatic Processing transition, using a filter on the order status assigned at checkout completion.
  • Use a delayed-capture payment gateway configuration (covered elsewhere) if the review should also delay actually charging the customer's card, not just delay fulfillment.
  • A dedicated order-approval plugin can add clearer explicit approve/reject buttons and staff notifications, rather than relying on staff remembering to check the On Hold queue.
  • Clear customer communication about the review step (a specific email explaining their order is pending confirmation) avoids confusion about why the order hasn't progressed immediately, which it otherwise would by default.

Implementing an Approval Workflow

  1. Decide the exact condition triggering review — all orders, a specific product category, orders above a value threshold.
  2. Configure the status/payment-capture behavior to hold at the review point rather than proceeding automatically.
  3. Set up clear staff notification for orders awaiting review, so they don't sit unnoticed.
  4. Communicate the review step to customers clearly, so it doesn't look like a broken or stuck order from their side.
